st: An ode to plants, between algorithms, CO2 capture and problems to solve

sec.t: ff.33.1 The philosophical and cognitive value of trees
sec.p: The connection between humans and plants has historically been very close. The tree has always been at the heart of many cultural aspects: from Adam and Eve to medieval theories of knowledge, all the way to search and optimisation algorithms (like the decision tree). Plant…

Plants, besides capturing CO2 during photosynthesis, keep it locked up for a shorter or longer period (in the carbon of bark and leaves). A Science study by the University of Zurich calculated that we could plant 0.9 million hectares, with a potential storage of 200 Gt…

sec.t: ff.33.3 Plants modified to capture CO2
sec.p: Plants are lazybones. Plants don't go all out to capture CO2. For example, even when there's plenty of sun, they slow their metabolism so as not to run out of other nutrients like water. So the conversion efficiency from CO2 to organic matter, which is then “held” as in the…

To close the circle between knowledge, algorithms and plants, let's talk about Plasmodium. It's a mould that has been used to find the shortest path connecting various regions (solving the famous Traveling Salesman Problem and showing great computational parallelisation skills).
